headline: NYC Funds Pet Food for Hungry Households Across All Five Boroughs
meta_description: New York City is investing $500,000 to stock pet food at 22 food pantries, helping struggling families keep their beloved animals.
summary_short: NYC is investing half a million dollars to provide free pet food at 22 pantries across all five boroughs, preventing families from having to surrender their pets.
body:
New York City is tackling a quiet crisis facing its poorest households: the impossible choice between feeding themselves and feeding their pets. The city has committed $500,000 to stock and distribute free pet food through 22 food pantries spanning all five boroughs, with supplies arriving within two weeks. The initiative recognizes a painful reality that animal welfare groups have documented for years—financial hardship is one of the leading reasons families surrender their pets to shelters, often as a last resort when every other option has run out.

Cassandra, a Brooklyn resident, knows this tension intimately. She has a three-year-old Shih Tzu named Teddy, and has often sacrificed portions of her own meals so he wouldn't go hungry. At The Campaign Against Hunger in Brooklyn, pantry director Tamara Dawson has witnessed the same pattern repeatedly: families arriving with their pets, struggling to make limited resources stretch across every mouth to feed. St. John's Bread and Life in Brooklyn received a $17,000 voucher through the program—a lifeline that comes as demand has surged following recent reductions to SNAP benefits, which ripple through household budgets in ways that affect pets too.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani framed the issue plainly: "No New Yorker should have to choose between feeding themselves and feeding their pets." By placing pet food directly within existing food pantries rather than creating separate systems, the city has built a solution that meets families where they already are. The program doesn't solve the affordability crisis itself, but it creates space—perhaps just enough breathing room for a struggling household to keep their companion close.

22 food pantries across all five boroughs now participating
Pet food supplies arriving within two weeks
